from.place: Proof input for the affine closed-immersion restriction: identify the induced inverse image with sheafification of evaluation along the lift, and evaluate it on weakly contractible basis objects.

title: Affine closed immersion inverse-image evaluation
statement: Let $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be a closed immersion of affine schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme]. Write $X_{\mathrm{app}}=\mathcal B_X$ and $Z_{\mathrm{app}}=\mathcal B_Z$ for the affine ind-etale bases [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] of their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use the functors $u,v$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties]. Let $i^{-1}$ be the inverse image for the ordinary base-change morphism of topoi [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and write $R_Z$ for restriction of sheaves to $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R_Z(i^{-1}F)$ is naturally isomorphic to the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$ of the presheaf $V\mapsto F(v(V))$. If $V$ is weakly contractible in $Z_{\mathrm{app}}$, then $(i^{-1}F)(V)\cong F(v(V))$, naturally in $F$ and such $V$. Here weakly contractible in a site means that every epimorphism $P\to Q$ of sheaves of sets on that site induces a surjection $P(V)\to Q(V)$; an epimorphism means a right-cancellable morphism.

proof.text: Use the already proved affine comparison instances from [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]: restriction RX and RZ along the full affine basis inclusions are equivalences. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties], v is cocontinuous and v is left adjoint to u, so u is continuous. Whisker the opposite adjunction on presheaves, compose with the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and restrict along the fully faithful inclusion of sheaves. This constructs L left adjoint to precomposition with u, where L is sheafification of precomposition with v. The base-change square gives the natural direct-image isomorphism beta: i_* followed by RX is isomorphic to RZ followed by u_*. Apply the proved generic inverse-mate lemma [lem-stage3-inverse-mate-equivalences] to beta and the ordinary inverse/direct-image adjunction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its inverse supplies precisely the first natural isomorphism. No explicit left Kan extension or new equivalence proof is needed.

For P equal to precomposition of an affine-basis sheaf H with v, use Mathlib Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem for the locally injective sheafification unit. Refine its covering sieve by a finite jointly surjective family using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Such a finite family belongs to the affine precoverage [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]: its scheme cover is quasi-compact by QuasiCompactCover.of_finite, and restriction of the full topology gives a covering generated sieve. By the covering-preservation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties], its v-image covers. Separatedness of H proves equality of the original sections. This proves unit injectivity without a contractibility assumption.

Reuse the fully proved sigmaCover, sigmaCover_ext and exists_sigmaCover_glue from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SigmaCover. They construct finite disjoint unions in the affine basis [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] and identify sheaf sections with arbitrary families of sections. Apply them to the subcanonical topology's uliftYoneda sheaves to prove that the standard Cofan on sigmaCover is a coproduct (Cofan.IsColimit.ofBijective). A left adjoint preserves this coproduct. For the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties], glue a family of sections on v(Uj) first on sigmaCover(v(Uj)), and restrict along the comparison arrow from v(sigmaCover(Uj)) supplied by the preserved coproduct. This proves leftAdjoint_sigmaCover_glue. It includes an empty indexing type. It requires no new filtered-colimit, finite-product or finite-family-geometry statement.

The affine topology is subcanonical by restricting the full subcanonical pro-etale topology along the fully faithful basis inclusion. For a surjective affine-basis arrow q: W -> V, use the already proved generate_singleton_mem_topology from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.Replete. The map uliftYoneda(q) is epi: use the sheaf Yoneda equivalence [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] to translate any two maps with equal precomposites into sections which agree after q, and conclude by separatedness for the singleton cover. The assumed surjectivity of evaluation on all epimorphisms lifts the identity of V to a section sigma of q. This is cover_split. For a finite jointly surjective family, source-library surjective_sigmaCoverπ supplies q. The empty case is included without any inhabitance assumption.

For any section s of sheafify(P) at a weakly contractible V, Mathlib Presheaf.imageSieve_mem for toSheafify gives a covering sieve of local lifts. Refine it finitely by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] and choose the lifts. Step 3 glues them to z in P(sigmaCover). Naturality of toSheafify and sigmaCover_ext show that the unit image of z equals the restriction of s along sigmaCoverπ. Step 4 supplies a section sigma of this map. Restrict z along sigma: functoriality and the section equation show its unit image is s. This is precomposition_unit_surjective. Pair this with step 2 for the restricted full-site sheaf RX(F). Together with step 1 these are exactly both clauses of affine_closed_inverseImage_evaluation, with its signature unchanged.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof follows the finite-cover and splitting argument of 09BL. Existing affine comparison, SigmaCover and Replete APIs replace the planned auxiliary geometry and algebra proofs; the proved inverse-mate tool supplies the adjunction comparison.

split_report.summary: Proved the two clauses of Stacks 09BL on the ind-etale bases: transported the ordinary direct image through dense-subsite restriction, evaluated its left Kan extension using v adjoint to u, and proved that sheafification does not change evaluation at a weakly contractible basis object. Wrote out finite disjoint unions, covering-representable epimorphisms and singleton-cover sections. No new nodes or statement changes.
